spec.description: Retrieve a list of withdrawal methods available for the user. Requires the `Funds permissions - Query` and `Funds permissions - Withdraw` API key permissions.

asset.description: Filter methods for a specific asset.

aclass.description: Filter methods for a specific asset class.

network.description: Filter methods for a specific network.

rebase_multiplier.description: Optional parameter for viewing xstocks data. `rebased` displays in terms of underlying equity; `base` displays in terms of SPV tokens.

response.description: Withdrawal methods available for the user.

items.title: WithdrawalMethod
items.description: One withdrawal method available for the user.

method_id.description: Unique identifier for the withdrawal method.

network.description: Name of the blockchain or network being withdrawn on.

minimum.description: Minimum net amount that can be withdrawn right now.

fee.title: WithdrawalMethodFee
fee.description: Fee details for a withdrawal method.

fee_percentage.description: Percentage fee (present instead of a flat fee for some methods).

limits.description: Rate limit details for this withdrawal method.

items.title: WithdrawalRateLimit
items.description: One rate limit rule for a withdrawal method.

limits.description: Limits keyed by the time window they apply to, in seconds.

additionalProperties.title: WithdrawalRateLimitWindow
additionalProperties.description: Rate limit usage for one time window.

maximum.description: Maximum amount allowed in this window.

used.description: Amount already used in this window.

notes: Upstream `requestBody` requires `nonce`; dropped from this schema since the core's `authed_request` (`core/transport/http.py`) injects a strictly-increasing nonce into every private call automatically -- it is never a caller-supplied parameter, matching the existing hand-written `deposit_methods(self, asset)` signature, which takes none.

`WithdrawalRateLimitWindow.maximum`/`.remaining`/`.used` are left as bare `string`, not `decimal-string`: the enclosing `limits` field is absent on all 776/776 real methods observed in `examples/default`, so there is no captured value to confirm the numbers are actually decimal-shaped -- never invent a format, per docs/spec/authoring.md rule 2/15.
